findings.title: Retry-limit deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second branch of this `OR` filters only on `retryCount`, so any `WorkflowReminder` method (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP) with a count above one will be deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. The retry cleanup condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or the outer query should constrain the method) so this endpoint cannot remove reminders owned by other delivery mechanisms.

findings.title: The condition permits a third scheduling attempt after two failures
findings.body: A reminder starts at `retryCount = 0`; its first and second failed attempts set the count to 1 and 2. On the next cron run `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is evaluated only before scheduling, so the row is deleted then, but it will already have been eligible for the second failure? More specifically, after the first failure it is retried; after the second failure it becomes 2 and is removed on the following run. This produces two attempts, but the cleanup timing leaves a persisted failed reminder. If the intended contract is to delete immediately after the second failed scheduling attempt, the failure update should delete at the limit or use a transaction/conditional operation. Otherwise the stated behavior is delayed until the next cron execution and failed rows remain available to other workers.

findings.title: Retry count updates can lose increments under overlapping cron runs
findings.body: The handler reads `reminder.retryCount` and later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. Two concurrent cron invocations can both select the same unscheduled reminder, both fail to schedule it, and both write the same value (for example, 1). This loses one failure, prevents the retry limit from being reached reliably, and both invocations can issue duplicate provider scheduling calls. Use an atomic database increment and claim/conditionally update the reminder before scheduling to ensure only one worker processes a reminder.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or generated message still retry forever
findings.body: Retry count is incremented only when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `sendTo` is empty (for example, an attendee has no SMS number) or template generation leaves `message` empty, this condition is skipped without marking the reminder scheduled, failed, or exhausted. The reminder therefore remains in every cron query until its scheduled date, retaining the infinite retry behavior this change is intended to stop. Treat an unsendable reminder as a failed attempt or explicitly delete/cancel it.
